notes:
Summary: Halcyon runs a low-latency adtech bidding stack. Primary ask: define and operationalize latency SLOs for Dedicated GPUs, align measurement (client vs server) and agree credits for misses. Wants deterministic p50/p95/p99 bounds for both non-streaming inference (reranking + embeddings) and streaming generation (chat + feature decode).

Key quoted requirements / context:
- CTO: "We cannot have tail spikes during auctions — >300ms is a hard stop for any path that touches the bid pipeline."
- Engineering: prefers VPC private control plane; no data leaves region without residency controls.

Measurement/definition concerns raised on call:
- Client-side end-to-end vs server-side processing time: Halcyon wants client-side (including network & LB) for product SLAs, but legal insists on server-side SLOs for vendor credits. Need mapping between the two (client_e2e = network_out + server_latency + network_back + client_parse).
- Streaming vs non-streaming: they define streaming as token-by-token (first-byte and per-token median), non-streaming as full-response latency (request->last-byte). Want separate SLOs and separate SLA credit buckets.
- Batching & KV cache warmup: P99 varies significantly between cold cache + batched requests. They asked for guidance on how to exclude scheduled maintenance windows and cache-warmup periods from rolling SLOs.

Instrumentation proposal discussed (engineering liked):
- Inject trace_id and call-timestamps at client send, server receive, model-first-byte, model-last-byte, server-send, client-last-byte. Capture both server-timestamped metrics and client-reported samples.
- Redwood Console will expose per-route p50/p95/p99 and first-byte vs last-byte metrics, plus a mapping view to correlate client_e2e vs server_latency.

SLA / reserved capacity notes:
- Halcyon expects a reserved pool sized for 8k QPS peak with 20% burst headroom. Initial Redwood sizing suggests ~16 A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline with autoscale burst taps for short auctions.
- Target SLOs proposed by AE (aligned with customer ask): non-streaming: p50 < 25ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms; streaming: first-byte p50 < 10ms, token-avg latency p95 < 40ms, token-avg p99 < 120ms.
- SLA negotiation: Halcyon wants contractual p99 <= 250ms 99.5% of monthly windows for core rerank route; Redwood counters with 99.9% for reserved capacity + credit ladder for sustained misses (>3h).

POC acceptance signals:
- 72-hour sustained test with production replay at 80% of peak QPS, p99 non-streaming <= 250ms and no functional errors per route.

Open action items captured in CRM:
- Agree canonical SLO definitions (client_e2e vs server_latency) and recording method (sampling vs continuous).
- Legal to agree data residency language and SLA credits (deadline 2026-03-25).
- SE to publish a short measurement spec doc and instrumentation snippet for Halcyon SDKs.
use_case_summary: Primary workload: real-time bidding (low-latency reranking + embeddings) and streaming chat for partner tools. Targets: sub-100ms p95 on hot routes, strict p99 tail limits for auction paths. Cost sensitivity: medium — will pay for reserved capacity if tail guarantees are reliable. Models: tuned open models + quantized variants; requires routing to cheaper variants when under capacity pressure.
measurement_spec: Canonical SLOs: p50/p95/p99 measured at server_response_last_byte for non-streaming routes; for streaming, measure first_byte_latency and token_interval_latency separately.
Client vs Server: record client_send_ts and server_receive_ts; present both client_e2e and server_latency in dashboards and maintain formula mapping.
Warm vs Cold: define warm-window = 5 minutes after first request to a model variant; statistics for SLOs will be computed both including and excluding cold-warm windows (POC decides final).
Aggregation: rolling 30-day window for SLA; 1-minute internal aggregation buckets for alerting; hourly rollups for weekly reports.
Sampling: continuous collection on reserved capacity POC; 1% downsample allowed for hosted long-term telemetry if needed by ingestion limits.
Error handling: failed requests (5xx) are counted separately and do not contribute to latency percentiles; but SLA credit triggers if error rate > 0.5% for >1h.
Traceability: require trace_id in headers (x-htl-trace) to tie client samples to server spans; Redwood will provide instrumentation snippet for common SDKs.
SLA credit triggers: negotiated ladder (e.g., 98.5% p99 -> 10% credit, 97% -> 25%); graceful fallback policy required to qualify for credits (must have canary fallback configured).
poc_plan: Week 0: instrument SDK + small synthetic smoke tests; validate trace propagation and metrics schema.
Week 1: production traffic replay at 30% peak to validate correctness and caching behavior.
Week 2: 72-hour sustained throughput test at 80% peak QPS with bursts; measure p50/p95/p99 for core routes and streaming first-byte metrics.
Acceptance criteria: p99 non-streaming <= 250ms, streaming token p99 <= 120ms, error rate <0.5%.
Deliverables: POC report (latency histograms, tail-analysis, kernel/quantization config used), Redwood sizing recommendation, proposed SLA language.
If pass: move to commercial sizing for dedicated pool + draft contract (target close month 2026-05).
